title: Deaths-in-custody (Office Of Victim Services And Justice Grants District Of Columbia)

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

The database or records of all Illinois law enforcement agencies deaths-in-custody up to the date this request is ultimately fulfilled, including all deaths-in-custody reported pursuant both Illinois state legislation (730 ILCS 210/3-5) and federal legislation (34 U.S.C. § 60105), as well as all data dictionaries, database scheme documentation or other documentation on the collection and organizatin of the data. 

I request these records in their native digital formats and not in formats that degrade the accessibility of the records, such as tabular data converted to PDF or Word files. If converting the native digital format to another high-fidelity format, such as CSV or Excel, please take care not to introduce formatting inconsistencies or errors, which can occur in the conversion process (for example, encoding errors or the inclusion of internal unescaped quotation marks in CSV files). Should the records above represent certain values as numeric codes or abbreviations that are not self-explanatory, we additionally request all records necessary to interpret those codes and abbreviations.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Dillon Bergin

title: Records of ICE custody or transfers following arrests in Henderson County, North Carolina

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Under the Freedom of Information Act (5 U.S.C. § 552), I request the following existing records maintained by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) concerning the  Henderson County Sherriff Office , North Carolina, from January 1, 2024, through October 19, 2026:

1. ICE detainers and custody requests: Records of detainers or requests for custody issued by ICE to the facility during the requested period.

2. Transfers to ICE custody: Records documenting transfers or handoffs from the facility to ICE custody, including the transfer date and receiving ICE office.

3. Existing summary records: Any existing logs, spreadsheets, or reports showing detainers issued to the facility or transfers from the facility to ICE custody.

If any records are withheld, please identify the applicable FOIA exemption. If ICE does not maintain responsive records, please advise whether another ICE component is likely to maintain them.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

title: Boston Police Department's Motor Vehicle Collisions Data: Officer & Traffic Stop Location Information

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

Under the Massachusetts Public Records Law, G.L. c. 66, § 10, I request the records described below. The requests relate to a traffic citation data set previously released by the Boston Police Department covering January 1, 2020, through June 30, 2025. That request’s traffic number is B002614-090924. Officer IDs below refer to the “Officer ID” field in that data set. I am not requesting home addresses, personal contact information, medical information, or disciplinary records for any officer, or names or identifying information of any motorist.

For each Officer ID listed in the attached “Officer_IDs_All_Assignment_History.csv” records showing the officer’s unit, district, or division assignment, with the effective start and end dates of each assignment, for any period between January 1, 2020 and June 30, 2025. If the IDs are invalid in the attached .csv, it is because they were invalid in the data released in response to request B002614-090924. If this information is kept in an electronic personnel or scheduling system, I request an export of those fields.

For each Officer ID in the attached “Officer_IDs_No_Name_or_Invalid.csv,”  I request you please provide records showing the officer’s name, badge number, rank, and POST Commission ID. For Officer IDs marked “ID value appears invalid – please explain” (including ID 0 and IDs above 1,000,000), I am requesting any and all records explaining what these values represent.

Any and all data dictionary, codebook, field definitions, or code lists for the traffic citation data set, including definitions for:

(a) race codes (UNK, UNKNWN, MIDEST, AFRICA, CAPVER, ASPAC, AMERIC, PACIFC, INDIAN, NATIVE, CAU);
(b) gender codes (NP, UNK);
(c) the “Location” field, including what the value “Boston” represents;
(d) the “Current Unit” field, including the date the employee data was extracted.

For each citation number listed in the attachment labeled “Citation_Numbers_Location_Boston.csv” (citations whose Location is recorded as “Boston”), any and all geolocation data and/or information, including but not limited to latitude and longitude, street addresses, intersections, neighborhoods, or police district recorded for the citation.

I request the records electronically in a machine-readable format (CSV or Excel) where they exist in that form, as permitted by G.L. c. 66, § 6A(d).

I also request that, if appropriate, fees be waived as we believe this request is in the public interest, as suggested but not stipulated by the recommendations of the Massachusetts Supervisor of Public Records. The requested documents will be made available to the general public free of charge as part of the public information service at MuckRock.com, and is not made for commercial usage.

I expect the request to be filled in an accessible format, including for screen readers, which provide text-to-speech for persons unable to read print. Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf image files as well as physical documents.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Nicole Liu
